item.title: One Pair Across Every Shot

turns.text: Make a realistic, silent 15-second widescreen story in three shots: a woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut drops a red scarf; a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks it up; he returns it and they smile. Both adults, on a quiet street. Show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout—no changing actors between cuts.

item.tests: Maintains two distinct generated facial identities across three story shots, including shots where either character is the focus.

answer_sheet.Character identities: An adult woman with a freckled face and red pixie cut, and an adult man with a shaved head and round glasses. Invent their faces but keep each identity unchanged across all three shots.
answer_sheet.Face visibility: Both faces must be clearly visible in every shot, including when the scarf is dropped and picked up.
answer_sheet.Story and setting: On a quiet street, the woman drops a red scarf, the man picks it up, and he returns it before they smile at each other.
answer_sheet.Length and format: One 15-second widescreen 16:9 video in three shots.
answer_sheet.Style and mood: Realistic live action, a small friendly encounter.
answer_sheet.Sound and text: Silent, with no captions, titles or dialogue.

must_haves: One assembled 15-second 16:9 film tells the story in three distinct shots.
The woman retains the same facial structure, freckles and red pixie cut in all three shots.
The man retains the same facial structure, shaved head and round glasses in all three shots; the two identities never merge or swap.
Both faces are clearly visible in every shot, not hidden by rear views, distant framing or object-only cutaways.
The red scarf is dropped by the woman, picked up by the man and returned to her in that order, ending with mutual smiles.
The film looks realistic and has no audible soundtrack.

turns.text: Could you make a realistic, silent story in three shots about a small encounter on a quiet street, with both people being adults? I like these little moments of kindness because they remind me of how much a brief interaction can mean. The woman has a freckled face and a red pixie cut, and she drops a red scarf in the first shot. The whole thing should be a 15-second widescreen video, and in the second shot a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks the scarf up. In the third shot, he returns it to her and they smile. My main worry is that the people might look like different actors after a cut. Please show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout, with no changing actors between cuts.
turns.agent:
I couldn’t generate the video because Magic Hour refused the first shot for **insufficient credits**. Nothing was created or charged.

The planned film is **15 seconds, silent, widescreen (16:9)**, with three 5-second shots in your requested order. The estimated cost is **360 credits**.

To reduce actor changes, the plan carries each shot’s final frame into the next and keeps both faces visible. That helps continuity, but it cannot guarantee exactly identical faces across cuts.

opening.text: Could you make a realistic, silent story in three shots about a small encounter on a quiet street, with both people being adults? I like these little moments of kindness because they remind me of how much a brief interaction can mean. The woman has a freckled face and a red pixie cut, and she drops a red scarf in the first shot. The whole thing should be a 15-second widescreen video, and in the second shot a man with a shaved head and round glasses picks the scarf up. In the third shot, he returns it to her and they smile. My main worry is that the people might look like different actors after a cut. Please show both faces clearly in every shot and keep exactly the same two faces throughout, with no changing actors between cuts.
